title: Store and retrieve an application secret
scenario: A payments service has a partner API key in its configuration file. Where should the replacement live, and which application identity may read it?
owner: Platform engineering sets the access policy with the service owner.
proof: Show an authorized service reading the intended secret and an unrelated service being denied. Confirm how versions are selected.

title: Deliver secrets to a running workload
scenario: A Kubernetes deployment needs a database password after each change. How does the running application pick up the replacement?
owner: Platform engineering owns delivery. The application owner verifies that the process loaded the new value.
proof: Trace a test change from the source to the consumer. Identify every persistent copy and whether the workload reads the change or must restart.

title: Give an application access to a team vault
scenario: A release job needs a secret from the team’s existing password-management platform. How can the job retrieve just what it needs without a person signing in?
owner: The vault administrator grants the machine identity access. The build owner manages the credentials used to start the job.
proof: Ask which vaults or projects the identity can read, how its own access can be revoked, and what remains accessible after revocation. Check issuer-side rotation separately.

title: Rotate a standing credential at its source
scenario: A database password has leaked. Updating its value in a vault is one step. Who changes the password on the database and gets all clients onto the replacement?
owner: The database or service owner controls the issuer. The application owner validates the cutover.
proof: Ask for the issuer-side result, proof that consumers switched and evidence that the old password stopped working. Check how partial failure is reported.

title: Issue short-lived database credentials
scenario: Ten services share a database login. Could each request time-limited access for its own role?
owner: The database owner defines privileges. The platform team operates the issuer and handles expiry failures.
proof: Use a test role to demonstrate issuance, expiry and revocation. Ask what happens to an existing database session and to revocation if the database is unavailable.

title: Replace a stored CI key with workload identity
scenario: A release pipeline holds a cloud account key. Can the cloud trust the pipeline identity and issue temporary credentials for each run?
owner: Identity and platform engineering define the trust policy and retire the old key once the cutover is proven.
proof: Show that the intended workflow can obtain access, another repository cannot, and the old stored key has been retired. This option applies to targets that accept federation.

title: Audit access after an exposure
scenario: A production secret was exposed last week. Can we show which identity retrieved it from the manager and whether anyone used it against the target service?
owner: Security operations reviews access events with the platform and target-service owners.
proof: Ask for one retrieval event with principal, time and resource. Verify log coverage and retention, then look separately for use at the target system.
